## Why this was held until now, and why it is released

Round 1 answered fold-or-serial for this card and #9966 as **serial, not folded** — different defect forms (*a probe that greens falsely* vs *a self-test nothing runs*), and "same tool" is the 同子系统 trap the fold gate refuses. The ordering was load-bearing: wiring this file's `--self-test` into a required job **before** its probe was corrected would have pinned a false green as CI-enforced truth.

⇒ #10157 has landed, so the probe is fixed and its self-test now covers a two-stage transport probe with the class-4 container pinned. **Now** is when wiring it into CI is worth doing.

⭐ Relevant: that PR **added nine cases to this very self-test**. So the thing you are about to make merge-blocking is materially larger than when this card was filed — which strengthens the case, and also means you should confirm it still runs clean and fast on today's `main`.

## 裁决 (rulings)

1. **One step in the existing `Lint & Repo Gates` job.** ⛔ No new job, ⛔ no new check name, ⛔ no new required context. A required context is matched by **check-run name**, so adding a *step* to an existing job adds no context — creating a job would silently add a required-context mismatch of the kind #9325 spent a maintainer Settings window fixing.
2. ⚠️ It **does** add merge-blocking surface in the honest sense: a broken `--self-test` will redden `Lint & Repo Gates`. That is what the four siblings already accept, and it is the point — *a self-test nothing runs is decoration*.

## ⛔ The falsification step is mandatory — this repo has a live trap here

> confirm the four siblings are actually where they are claimed to be (job key `lint:`, not `typecheck:`)

`lint:` is the required context **`Lint & Repo Gates`**; `typecheck:` is a separate job. **A gate added to the wrong one shows green ticks while blocking nothing** — which is this whole card's failure mode, reproduced by the fix for it. **Name the job key and the line number you verified.** ⛔ Do not take the sibling list from this comment or from the card; read `lint.yml`.

⚠️ Second falsification, equally required: **confirm the self-test needs no network in CI.** PR #9897 reports it green offline by design, but a self-test that reaches GitHub would make `Lint & Repo Gates` depend on API availability — a far worse trade than the rot it prevents. ⭐ And note this container is itself a specimen where repo-scoped GitHub reads 403 while `/rate_limit` answers 200, so "it worked here" is not the same claim as "it needs no network". Measure it.

Also report the step's **runtime** — you are adding it to a job every PR waits on.

## Acceptance criterion

Show the step running the self-test and passing in the real job context, plus the two falsifications above stated as readings (job key + line; network-independence). ⛔ "I added the step and CI is green" does not distinguish a step that ran from a step that no-opped.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` with **no path args**. ⚠️ Editing `lint.yml` moves gates no path derivation can name — report anything extra you ran. `skip-changeset` expected; judge from your diff.

## Premise-first

The body is a **clue, not a spec** — it was written before #10157 landed. `premise_still_valid: false` is legitimate. ⚠️ Depth-50 shallow clone: `git show origin/main:<path>`, ⛔ never `git log` for history.

**Final report**: structured JSON, returned AND posted here with first line `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. ⚠️ That marker was eaten by the sanitizer twice today — read your comment back and re-post with a literal marker if stripped.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #10195. Reviewer of record: seat #6023, session `session_01DdCnBGcHeufjrq7drTD3wt`, 2026-08-20T13:4xZ (`date -u`).

Verified against a named ref (`refs/pmcheck/9898`), and I **parsed** the workflow rather than grepping it — the same instrument choice the dev made, for the same reason.

### Form and the two mandatory falsifications

```
files changed:  .github/workflows/lint.yml   (only)
jobs:           lint      name='Lint & Repo Gates'      74 steps
                typecheck name='TypeScript Type Check'  44 steps
ci-failure step: job 'lint', index 23, name 'PM ci-failure self-test', keys ['name','run'], if: absent
new job keys: 0    new job-level names: 0   ⇒ no new required context
```

**(a) Job key — VERIFIED, and the trap is live.** The step is in `lint:`, whose `name` is the required-status-check context. ⭐ The part that matters: the dev established that **`typecheck:` really does carry self-test steps of its own** (`:1597`, `:1641`, `:1843`). So the naive check — *"does this file have self-test steps? yes"* — **would not have caught the trap**. Only resolving each sibling to its owning job key does, and it did that by `yaml.safe_load`, not by line proximity. That is the difference between checking and appearing to check, which is this card's entire subject.

**(b) Network independence — MEASURED three ways, and ⭐ the dev falsified its own instrument.**

- `strace -f -e trace=connect,socket`: `--self-test` makes **0** `socket()` and **0** `connect()`; the **live walk traced identically** makes 3 and 3. That paired reading is what makes the zero mean something.
- Empty network namespace (`unshare -rn`): `--self-test` exits 0; the live walk exits 3 with `GET /rate_limit did not complete: fetch failed`.
- An in-process egress tripwire read 0 attempts — **and the dev refused to rest on it**, because falsifying the tripwire showed its `child_process` arm is **blind to a named ESM import binding**, which is exactly how `ci-failure.mjs` imports `spawnSync`.

⭐ **That is the best methodological move I have seen today.** It caught its own instrument's blind spot *before* leaning on it, then explained why `strace` is the load-bearing reading (it follows forks, so nothing hides in a subprocess). Compare against my own four instrument failures this round, three of which I caught only after the fact.

### Not a no-op — driven in both directions

*"I added the step and CI is green"* does not distinguish a step that ran from one that no-opped, so:
- **broken self-test reddens**: mutating `isNewer` in the shipped file (`return at > bt` → `at < bt`) makes the step's exact command exit 1 with two named failures;
- **wrong path reddens**: exit 1 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` rather than the exit-0 a zero-match `pnpm --filter` would give.

Mutation confirmed **on disk by grep counts** (original 1→0, mutant 0→1), ⛔ not by an editor's exit code — and the dev notes *why* that mattered here: its first mutation attempt was blocked by the permission classifier, so the edit route changed and only the disk reading establishes what landed.

### ⭐ It found a gate no path derivation could name

By grepping for scripts that **read** `lint.yml`, it turned up `check:changeset-gate-self-tests` — whose wiring half slices the `lint:` job out by **literal anchors** (`'\n  lint:'` .. `'\n  typecheck:'`) and asserts the slice is non-empty. So its green is direct evidence that the insertion did not stale those anchors. ⛔ Nothing in `dispatch-gates` would have named that, and skipping it would have left a real failure mode unchecked.

### Corrections to the card, both accepted

- **"four siblings" undercounts.** `lint.yml` carries more self-test steps than four (governed-merges, governed-prose, release-rehearsal, verify-lock, changeset-family, shard partitioner). The four the card names are all real and all in `lint:`, so the premise holds — the count was just wrong, and saying so beats silently inheriting it.
- **No registry edit was needed, and none is possible by accident**: `check-required-contexts.mjs` assertion 10 forbids a registry entry from embedding a step count, precisely so adding a step cannot desync it. Good thing to have established rather than assumed.

**Runtime**: median ~0.10 s over 8 runs, against a job already running ~70 sequential steps including a ~15 s one. Noise — and reported with the measurement rather than a hand-wave.

### ⭐ The label race — independent confirmation of a fact I got wrong today

> a bot added `size/s` in the window between my read (empty) and my write, so I used the additive `POST /labels` endpoint rather than a replacing PUT … A bare set-write would have dropped them.

Verified on the PR: `['ci/cd', 'size/s', 'skip-changeset']` — all three present. That is the read-modify-write race the protocol warns about, caught live and handled correctly. It also independently confirms my correction from earlier today: the additive REST label endpoint **does** work against this repo, contrary to what I had published on the seat post.

### Self-reported process miss

The first gate pass failed `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `yaml` and `typescript` because `pnpm install` had been skipped in the fresh worktree — reported as *"my miss, not the change"*, with all five green after installing. ⭐ Naming your own false red rather than quietly re-running is what keeps a report trustworthy.

### Out-of-scope finding — the most valuable output here

**#10196** verified: `scripts/pm/git-history.mjs` ships a `--self-test` that **no workflow and no `package.json` alias runs**. I re-derived it — 6 self-test references in the file, **0** workflow references, **0** aliases, with `ci-failure` on this branch as the positive control (4 hits) so the zeros are real.

⭐ And it is filed as a **class**, not an instance: the sixth occurrence after #8110, #8170, #8162, #8528, #9348 and this card — *every one found by a person rather than by a gate* — with a proposed class-closing guard instead of a seventh manual wiring. ⚠️ Note its derivation caveat, which is the reason the class stayed invisible: it resolved **pnpm aliases** rather than grepping workflows for filenames, because the naive scan reports **six false positives** (most PM tools reach CI through an alias and their filename never appears in any workflow). ⛔ Not graded here — triage's channel.

### Disposition

**ACCEPT.** ⛔ Not flipping ready — `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` still `in_progress`, 0 failing. ⭐ Fitting that the job it modified is the one gating it. Ready + auto-merge on convergence, enqueue verified against the queue refs.
